draft.title: Subcultures
card: A subculture is a group within a larger society that has its own values, styles and ways of behaving. These differ from those of the wider society.
Members share things such as dress, language, music, interests and beliefs. These shared features help members recognise each other and feel they belong.
Skaters and gamers are examples. Members still live in the wider society and share much of its culture, such as its language and laws.
Being different does not make a subculture opposed to society. Many subcultures are harmless, and some become part of mainstream culture over time.
draft.remember: A subculture is a group inside a society with its own values and styles, but it is still part of that society.

a.q: Which description best fits a subculture?
opts: A group within a society with its own values and styles
A group that has left a society to live apart from it
A group that follows every norm of the wider society
A group set up by a government to enforce its laws
a.why: A subculture has values and styles that differ from the wider society, yet its members still live within that society. The option about leaving society is wrong because subcultures remain part of the society around them.
a.clue: A subculture sits inside a larger society and is different from it.

b.q: Dana joins a local skate group in Newcastle. Members share slang, clothing and a love of skating, and they also go to school and follow Australian law. Why is the group a subculture?
opts: It has its own values and styles within the wider society
It rejects the laws and institutions of Australian society
It was formed because its members were punished by others
It has no shared values beyond a single hobby or interest
b.why: The group has its own slang, dress and values while its members stay part of Australian society. It is not defined by rejecting the law, because the card says being different does not mean being opposed to society.
b.clue: Look at what the group shares and where its members still belong.

a.best: A group within a society with its own values and styles

b.best: It has its own values and styles within the wider society
